name: Maya Thompson, PICU: new-onset type 1 diabetes in severe DKA

caseMeta.title: Pediatric ICU to adolescent unit: new-onset type 1 diabetes in severe diabetic ketoacidosis (3 days, checkpoints at every 0700 and 1900)
caseMeta.studentLevel: BSN / ADN pediatrics or medical-surgical (upper level)
learningObjectives: Recognize severe DKA in a teen with new-onset type 1 diabetes (polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, vomiting, Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath, drowsiness) and interpret the glucose, pH, bicarbonate, anion gap, beta-hydroxybutyrate and corrected sodium.

Manage a pediatric DKA protocol safely: weight-based fluids without repeated boluses, insulin infusion 0.1 unit/kg/h with no bolus, the two-bag dextrose system, potassium and phosphate rules, hourly glucose and neuro checks.
Recognize and act on the warning signs of cerebral edema (headache, falling heart rate, rising blood pressure, vomiting, change in alertness) and give mannitol by order.

Carry out the transition to basal-bolus subcutaneous insulin with overlap, prevent and treat hypoglycemia, and teach a new diagnosis to a teen and her parents (carbohydrate counting, insulin pens, glucagon, sick-day and ketone rules, CGM, school plan).

orders.name: sodium chloride 0.9% bolus (ED)
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mL (10 mL/kg) IV Once over 30 minutes.

orders.name: sodium chloride 0.9% infusion (ED, before potassium could be added)
orders.instructions: Administer 150 mL/h IV Continuous.
orders.rationale: Deficit + maintenance: maintenance 86 mL/h (Holliday-Segar for 48.6 kg) + 8% deficit (3,900 mL) minus the 500 mL bolus over 48 h (71 mL/h) = 157 mL/h, rounded to 150 mL/h (3.1 mL/kg/h, under 2 x maintenance). No potassium yet: K 5.6 at 0220 and not yet voided.

medication.freqKey: Continuous

orders.name: insulin regular (HUMULIN R) 100 units in 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL (1 unit/mL) infusion - DKA
orders.instructions: Run at 0.1 unit/kg/h = 4.9 units/h on its own pump; join at the port closest to the patient. Prime/flush the new tubing with 20 mL of the insulin solution (insulin sticks to tubing). Independent double check at every bag/rate change. Do NOT stop or lower the insulin to treat a falling glucose: add dextrose with the two-bag system instead. Call the PICU provider if glucose is under 150 mg/dL on Bag B 100% (D10), glucose falls more than 100 mg/dL in 1 hour, or potassium is under 3.0. Continue unchanged on transfer to the PICU. The rate may only be lowered (never below 0.05 unit/kg/h = 2.4 units/h) by a provider order.
orders.rationale: Severe DKA, new-onset type 1 diabetes. Started 0400, more than 1 hour after IV fluids began (cerebral edema precaution). NO insulin bolus (pediatric protocol).
nursingConsiderations: Hourly POC glucose and neuro check; strict I&O.
High-alert drug: two-nurse check of drug, concentration, rate and patient.
Stop only by order, at least 1-2 hours after the first subcutaneous basal insulin dose.

medication.importantInfo: Insulin stops ketone production; the acidosis (pH, bicarbonate, anion gap, beta-hydroxybutyrate) is the target, not the glucose. Insulin moves potassium into the cells: the blood potassium falls quickly even though the body is low on potassium.
medication.freqKey: Continuous (DKA protocol)

orders.name: Admit to Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), room PICU-4: severe diabetic ketoacidosis, new-onset type 1 diabetes. Attending: E. Whitford, MD (days) / J. Kowalski, MD (nights)
Full Code
Vital signs every 1 hour with continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring and pulse oximetry
orders.instructions: Call for HR under 70 or over 140, SBP over 130 or DBP over 85 (her baseline 108/66), RR under 12, SpO2 under 94%, temperature 100.4 F or higher.

orders.name: NEURO CHECKS EVERY 1 HOUR (GCS, pupils, headache, behavior) - cerebral edema watch
orders.instructions: Call the PICU provider IMMEDIATELY (and stay with the patient) for ANY of: new or worse headache; heart rate falling 20 or more not explained by sleep or better hydration; rising blood pressure; vomiting again; new confusion, restlessness, irritability or harder to wake; incontinence; pupil change or new double vision; SpO2 drop. Do not give acetaminophen for a headache before the provider assesses her.
orders.rationale: Highest risk: new-onset diabetes, pH 7.04, pCO2 16, BUN 28; usual onset 4-12 hours after treatment starts.
nursingConsiderations: Head of bed 30 degrees, head midline.
Mannitol and 3% saline orders are active (PRN); the drugs are in the PICU cabinet.

orders.name: Strict intake and output: measure every void (urinal hat), no catheter unless unable to void; daily weight at 0600 on the same scale
Bed rest, head of bed 30 degrees; up to the bathroom/commode with 1 assist only
NPO except ice chips (all fluid by IV during DKA treatment)
Point-of-care glucose every 1 hour while on the insulin infusion
orders.instructions: Use the result to set the two-bag ratio (see the Bag A / Bag B orders). Call for glucose under 150 on D10, a fall of more than 100 mg/dL in 1 hour, or under 70.

orders.name: BMP, magnesium, phosphorus, venous blood gas and beta-hydroxybutyrate every 4 hours (0830, 1230, 1630, 2030, 0030, 0430) until DKA resolves
orders.instructions: Draw from the right forearm IV (saline lock: waste 3 mL first) - never from the arm with the insulin infusion. Ionized calcium with the 1630 and 0430 gases (potassium phosphate running). Call for K under 3.5 or over 5.5, phosphorus under 1.0, sodium falling, pH not improving.
orders.rationale: DKA resolves when venous pH is 7.30 or higher, bicarbonate 18 or higher and beta-hydroxybutyrate under 0.6 (anion gap closed, 12 or lower).

orders.name: POTASSIUM RULES for the IV fluids
orders.instructions: Potassium is added only while K is under 5.5 AND the patient is voiding. Usual 40 mEq/L (half as KCl, half as potassium phosphate). Maximum 0.5 mEq/kg/h (24 mEq/h). Call for K under 3.5 or over 5.5, no void in 4 hours, or new ECG changes (peaked T; flat T with U waves).

orders.name: Pediatric endocrinology consult: new-onset type 1 diabetes in severe DKA
Pharmacy: DKA protocol dose check (weight 48.6 kg), no home medications
mannitol 20% injection (CEREBRAL EDEMA - keep available)
orders.frequency: PRN for signs of cerebral edema, ordered by the PICU provider at the bedside; may repeat in 30 minutes if no response
orders.instructions: Give over 10-15 minutes through a filter. Usual first dose 0.5 g/kg = 24 g (120 mL). Expect a large urine output: measure it.
orders.rationale: High risk of cerebral edema (new onset, pH 7.04, pCO2 16, BUN 28).

medication.importantInfo: First choice for DKA-related cerebral edema; 3% saline is the alternative. Do not wait for a CT scan to treat.
medication.freqKey: PRN for signs of cerebral edema, ordered by the PICU provider at the bedside; may repeat in 30 minutes if no response

orders.name: insulin glargine (LANTUS) SoloStar pen
orders.instructions: Give 0745 Tue with the insulin infusion still running; the infusion stops at 0915 (1.5 hours of overlap). Never mix with other insulin. Rotate sites (abdomen, thigh, back of arm).
orders.rationale: Total daily dose estimate about 0.9-1 unit/kg/day (about 44-48 units) for a pubertal teen after DKA; basal about 40-45% = 20 units (0.41 unit/kg).

medication.importantInfo: Basal insulin lasts about 24 hours with no peak. Stopping the IV insulin without basal insulin on board lets ketones come back within hours.

notes.author: C. Huang, RN
notes.summary: Arrived 0205 with mother: 5 weeks of thirst, peeing a lot and weight loss; vomiting since Sunday; deep fast breathing, fruity breath, drowsy. POC glucose HI. ESI 2, to resuscitation bay.
notes.body:
**Arrival 0205** by private car with her mother (Danielle Thompson). Walked in with help.

**Story (mother and Maya)**
- About 5 weeks of being very thirsty (2-3 large sports drinks plus water every day), peeing "all the time", up 3-4 times a night; wet the bed once last week.
- Lost weight: 54.2 kg at her sports physical in August. Tired, falling asleep in class.
- Saturday: belly ache and nausea. Sunday from about 0900: vomited 6 times, could not keep fluids down. Sunday evening: breathing deep and fast, "really sleepy". Mother brought her in when she could not stay awake to talk.
- No fever, no diarrhea, no cough, no urinary burning. No known diabetes. No medicines. No allergies.

**Triage 0210**
T 99.1 F, HR 134, BP 108/64, RR 32 deep and regular (Kussmaul), SpO2 99% room air, pain 6/10 upper belly. Weight 48.6 kg (standing, with help). GCS 14 (E3 V5 M6). Fruity (acetone) breath. Dry cracked lips, no tears, capillary refill 3-4 seconds, hands cool.

**POC glucose 0225: HI (over 600).**

ESI 2. To resuscitation bay 2; Dr. Adeyemi at the bedside 0218. Two IVs and labs ordered (DKA order set).

notes.summary: Sinus tachycardia 128, PR 136 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 452 ms. Tall, narrow, peaked T waves V2-V4 (potassium 5.6 at 0220).
notes.body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 128 bpm. PR 136 ms. QRS 82 ms. QT/QTc 310/452 ms.

**Interpretation**
Sinus tachycardia. Tall, narrow, peaked T waves in V2 to V4. P waves present, PR and QRS normal: no signs of severe hyperkalemia. QTc borderline long (common in DKA; recheck after treatment). No ST changes.

**Context**
Severe DKA, potassium 5.6 at 0220 (resulted 0300). Insulin will move potassium into the cells quickly: the body is actually low on potassium. Add potassium to the fluids once K is under 5.5 and she is voiding.

notes.title: ED Provider Note - New-Onset Type 1 Diabetes in Severe DKA
notes.author: N. Adeyemi, MD
notes.summary: Severe DKA at diagnosis of type 1 diabetes: pH 7.04, bicarbonate 5, anion gap 28, BHB 7.8, glucose 612, about 8% dehydrated, AKI. One 10 mL/kg bolus, insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h from 0400 without bolus, two-bag fluids with potassium from 0545. PICU accepted.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Vomiting, belly pain and fast breathing.

**HPI**
16-year-old previously healthy girl with about 5 weeks of polydipsia, polyuria, nocturia, one episode of bedwetting, fatigue and weight loss (54.2 kg in August, 48.6 kg today: about 10%). Vomiting since Sunday morning, then deep fast breathing and drowsiness. No fever, diarrhea, cough or urinary symptoms. LMP 3 weeks ago.

**Exam**
Drowsy, GCS 14 (E3 V5 M6), oriented to person and place, no focal signs, pupils 4 mm equal and reactive. Kussmaul respirations 32, fruity breath, lungs clear. HR 134, BP 108/64, capillary refill 3-4 s, cool hands, dry mucous membranes, no tears. Abdomen soft, diffusely tender, no guarding.

**Results (drawn 0220, before insulin)**
- Venous gas: **pH 7.04, pCO2 16, HCO3 4.2**; lactate 2.4.
- BMP: Na 131, K 5.6, Cl 98, CO2 5, BUN 28, creatinine 1.3, **glucose 612**, Ca 9.6, Mg 2.4, phosphorus 6.8. **Anion gap 28.** Corrected sodium (1.6 per 100 mg/dL glucose over 100) about 139. Measured osmolality 309; effective osmolality about 296.
- **Beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.8.** Lipase 41. WBC 18.4 (stress response; no fever or source), Hgb 15.1, Hct 45.2 (hemoconcentration).
- Urine (0330): glucose over 1,000, ketones large, SG 1.030; **hCG negative**.
- ECG 0300: sinus tachycardia 128, peaked T waves, QTc 452.
- Repeat 0430: pH 7.07, CO2 6, K 4.7, glucose 520, anion gap 25, beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.1.
- Sent: HbA1c, C-peptide, GAD65, IA-2, ZnT8 and insulin autoantibodies (before insulin), TSH and free T4, celiac screen.

**Assessment**
Severe DKA (pH under 7.1, bicarbonate under 5) at diagnosis of type 1 diabetes. About 8% dehydration with prerenal AKI (creatinine may also read high from ketones in the assay). High risk of cerebral edema: new onset, severe acidosis, low pCO2, high BUN.

**Treatment (pediatric DKA protocol, ISPAD 2022)**
- One 0.9% saline bolus 10 mL/kg (500 mL) over 30 min at 0240 for poor perfusion; not in shock, so no further boluses.
- Deficit + maintenance over 48 h: maintenance 86 mL/h + (3,900 mL deficit - 500 mL bolus) / 48 h = 71 mL/h = 157, **ordered 150 mL/h** (under 2 x maintenance).
- **Regular insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h = 4.9 units/h from 0400** (more than 1 h after fluids began), **no insulin bolus.**
- Potassium: none while K 5.6 and not voiding; voided 0330, K 4.7 at 0430: **two-bag system with potassium 40 mEq/L (half KCl, half potassium phosphate) ordered 0530**, starting 0545. Bag B (D10) starts when glucose is under 300.
- No bicarbonate (not indicated; raises cerebral edema risk).
- Ondansetron 4 mg at 0235.

**Disposition**
Discussed with Dr. Kowalski (PICU), accepted 0520. Pediatric endocrinology to see in the morning. Mother updated at the bedside.

notes.author: J. Kowalski, MD
notes.summary: Admit to PICU: severe DKA at diagnosis of type 1 diabetes, about 8% dehydrated, high cerebral edema risk. Continue insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h and two-bag fluids 150 mL/h; hourly glucose and neuro checks; labs every 4 hours; mannitol and 3% saline available.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
New-onset type 1 diabetes with severe DKA.

**History of present illness**
See ED note. 5 weeks of polyuria, polydipsia, nocturia and 10% weight loss; 1 day of vomiting; Kussmaul breathing and drowsiness. In the ED: saline 500 mL (10 mL/kg), insulin 4.9 units/h from 0400 with no bolus, two-bag fluids from 0545.

**Past history**
Healthy. Term birth. Immunizations up to date, including influenza vaccine (October 2026 school clinic). No surgeries. No medicines, no supplements. **No known drug allergies.** Menarche at 12; LMP 3 weeks ago.

**Family history**
Maternal aunt: Hashimoto thyroiditis. Paternal grandfather: type 2 diabetes. No type 1 diabetes, celiac disease or early heart disease known.

**Social history**
Lives with her mother (Danielle, school cafeteria manager), father (Kevin, long-haul truck driver, driving home tonight) and brother Eli (11). Junior at Westbrook High School, honor roll, club volleyball. Learner's driving permit. Insurance through her mother's school district job. Confidential adolescent (HEADSS) interview deferred until she is more alert.

**Exam (0615)**
T 98.8 F, HR 120, BP 112/70, RR 28 deep, SpO2 99% RA. Weight 48.6 kg, height 163 cm, BMI 18.3. Drowsy but rousable to voice, GCS 14, oriented to person and place, pupils 4 mm equal and reactive, no papilledema seen, moves all limbs, no focal deficits. Fruity breath. Lungs clear. Tachycardic, no murmur, capillary refill 2-3 s. Abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness. Dry mucous membranes. Thin. Tanner 5.

**Results**
See ED note (0220 and 0430 panels). POC glucose 441 at 0600.

**Assessment**
16-year-old with **severe DKA at diagnosis of type 1 diabetes**, improving slowly on treatment (glucose falling about 55 mg/dL per hour; anion gap 28 to 25). About 8% dehydrated, prerenal AKI. **High cerebral edema risk.**

**Plan**
1. **DKA**: continue regular insulin **0.1 unit/kg/h (4.9 units/h)**; do not lower it for glucose, use dextrose. **Two-bag system**, total 150 mL/h; ratio by hourly POC glucose (table in the order). Target glucose 150-250 while the acidosis clears. BMP, Mg, phosphorus, venous gas and beta-hydroxybutyrate every 4 h (0830, 1230, 1630, 2030, 0030, 0430). Resolution: pH 7.30 or higher, bicarbonate 18 or higher, beta-hydroxybutyrate under 0.6.
2. **Cerebral edema**: neuro checks every hour; HOB 30 degrees; no further boluses unless in shock; NPO except ice chips; **mannitol 20% 0.5-1 g/kg and 3% saline 2.5-5 mL/kg ordered PRN**. RN to call immediately for headache, falling heart rate, rising BP, vomiting or any change in alertness.
3. **Potassium/phosphate**: K 40 mEq/L in both bags (half as potassium phosphate) while K under 5.5 and voiding; maximum 0.5 mEq/kg/h. Cardiac monitor.
4. **Fluids/renal**: strict I&O, daily weight 0600. Creatinine expected to normalize with fluids.
5. Endocrinology consult in the morning; pharmacy dose check.
6. Mother at the bedside; father arriving tonight. Social work in the morning.
7. Full Code.

notes.title: Pharmacy Note - DKA Protocol Dose Check
notes.author: V. Shah, PharmD
notes.summary: Weight 48.6 kg. Insulin infusion 4.9 units/h (0.1 unit/kg/h), two-bag fluids, potassium 0.12 mEq/kg/h at 150 mL/h (40 mEq/L), mannitol and 3% saline doses checked. No home medicines.
notes.body:
**Medication history**
No prescription or over-the-counter medicines, supplements or energy drinks (large regular sports drinks daily for weeks, now stopped). Immunizations up to date per the state registry, including influenza (October 2026).

**Dosing weight** 48.6 kg (ED scale).

**Checked**
- Regular insulin 100 units/100 mL (1 unit/mL): **0.1 unit/kg/h = 4.86, ordered 4.9 units/h (4.9 mL/h)**. Lowest rate allowed while acidotic: 0.05 unit/kg/h = 2.4 units/h. No bolus (correct for pediatrics).
- Two-bag fluids: 0.9% saline base, potassium 40 mEq/L (20 KCl + 20 mEq K as potassium phosphate = 13.6 mmol phosphate/L). At 150 mL/h: potassium 6 mEq/h = **0.12 mEq/kg/h** (maximum 0.5). Phosphate 2 mmol/h.
- Fluid rate 150 mL/h = 3.1 mL/kg/h = 1.7 x maintenance (86 mL/h). Acceptable (under 2 x).
- **Mannitol 20%**: 0.5 g/kg = **24 g = 120 mL**; 1 g/kg = 48 g = 240 mL. Over 10-15 min with an in-line filter; 20% bags (250 mL) stored warm in the PICU cabinet so crystals do not form. **3% saline** 2.5-5 mL/kg = 120-240 mL.
- Dextrose 10% 2 mL/kg = 100 mL for glucose under 70. Ondansetron 4 mg (0.08 mg/kg; maximum single dose). QTc 452 ms on the 0300 ECG: acceptable; recheck if repeated doses.
- Acetaminophen 650 mg = 13.4 mg/kg (hold for headache until the provider assesses).

**Recommendations**
- Insulin bag change every 24 h with new primed tubing; independent double checks at every rate change.
- Watch calcium and magnesium with phosphate (Ca 9.2 at 0430).
- Will help with pen insulin teaching and insurance checks when she transitions.

notes.author: E. Whitford, MD
notes.summary: Improving slowly: pH 7.14, bicarbonate 7, anion gap 23, BHB 5.2 at 0830; glucose 287 at 0900 -> Bag B started (D5). K 3.9. HbA1c 12.8%. Neuro checks normal. Continue protocol; watch for cerebral edema in the next hours.
notes.body:
**Subjective**
Sleepy but answers questions; asks for water. Mild belly ache, no headache. Mother at the bedside.

**Objective**
Monitor at 0900 (per RN): sinus tachycardia 110s, BP 116/70, RR 24 still deep, SpO2 99% RA, afebrile. GCS 14-15 on hourly checks, pupils equal and brisk. Voided 220 mL at 0800.

POC glucose: 386 (0700), 334 (0800), 287 (0900). **Bag B started 0905 at 50/50 (D5)** per the table.

Labs 0830: **pH 7.14**, pCO2 19, HCO3 6.2; Na 135, **K 3.9**, Cl 105, **CO2 7**, BUN 22, creatinine 1.0, glucose 318, phosphorus 2.6, Mg 2.0. **Anion gap 23** (28 at 0220). **Beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.2** (7.8). Corrected sodium about 138.5 (139 at 0220: steady).

**HbA1c 12.8%** (resulted 0900): months of high glucose. TSH 2.1, free T4 1.0 (normal).

**Assessment and plan**
- **Severe DKA, improving at the expected rate**: beta-hydroxybutyrate falling about 0.4 per hour, gap closing. Continue insulin 4.9 units/h; two-bag ratio per glucose; total 150 mL/h. Next labs 1230.
- **Potassium 3.9 and falling** with insulin: continue 40 mEq/L; call for under 3.5.
- **Phosphorus 2.6 and falling** (6.8 at 0220): expected; potassium phosphate in the bags.
- **Cerebral edema watch**: she is in the highest-risk window (usually 4-12 h after treatment starts). Corrected sodium should stay steady or rise as glucose falls; a falling corrected sodium is a warning sign. Hourly neuro checks; call for any headache.
- AKI improving (creatinine 1.3 to 1.0).
- Social work consult placed (father traveling, new chronic illness). Endocrinology to see this morning.

notes.title: Pediatric Endocrinology Consult - New-Onset Type 1 Diabetes
notes.author: R. Banerjee, MD
notes.summary: New-onset type 1 diabetes (HbA1c 12.8%) presenting in severe DKA. Agree with the protocol. Transition to basal-bolus insulin once the acidosis resolves and she can eat (likely Tuesday breakfast). Antibodies, C-peptide and celiac pending. Teaching plan for Maya and both parents.
notes.body:
**Reason for consult**
New-onset diabetes with severe DKA.

**History**
As in the H&P. Classic symptoms for about 5 weeks, 10% weight loss, sugary sports drinks for thirst. No family history of type 1 diabetes; maternal aunt with Hashimoto thyroiditis. BMI 18.3; no acanthosis nigricans.

**Data**
HbA1c 12.8%. 0830: pH 7.14, bicarbonate 7, anion gap 23, beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.2, K 3.9. TSH 2.1, free T4 1.0. POC glucose 262 at 1000 on D5. Pending: GAD65, IA-2, ZnT8 and insulin autoantibodies (drawn 0220, before insulin), C-peptide, tissue transglutaminase IgA with total IgA.

**Assessment**
**New-onset type 1 diabetes** (lean teen, DKA, high HbA1c; antibodies expected positive), presenting in severe DKA. Thyroid normal.

**Recommendations**
1. Continue the PICU DKA protocol. Do not stop or lower the insulin infusion for glucose; dextrose instead.
2. **Transition** when pH is 7.30 or higher, bicarbonate 18 or higher, beta-hydroxybutyrate under 0.6 and she can eat. Plan: insulin glargine about 0.4 unit/kg (about 20 units) given 1-2 hours before stopping the infusion, plus insulin lispro with the first meal (carbohydrate ratio about 1 unit per 12 g; correction about 1 unit per 40 mg/dL over 150). I will write the orders.
3. **Education** (diabetes educator, dietitian): survival skills first (glucose checks, insulin pens, low glucose treatment, glucagon, ketones and sick-day rules), then carbohydrate counting. Both parents need to give an injection before discharge. CGM before discharge (insurance check).
4. School plan: Diabetes Medical Management Plan for the school nurse; 504 plan.
5. Screen for other autoimmune disease: thyroid done, celiac pending.

Discussed with Maya and her mother: this is not caused by anything they did. Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease; it needs insulin for life, and people with it do everything other people do, including volleyball and driving.

notes.title: PICU Event Note - Possible Cerebral Edema
notes.author: E. Whitford, MD
notes.summary: 1130: new headache 7/10, vomited, more drowsy and confused (GCS 13), HR 110 to 72, BP 134/92. Treated as cerebral edema: mannitol 24 g IV 1140, fluids cut to 100 mL/h, HOB 30. Better by 1215 (GCS 15, HR 96, BP 118/74). Corrected sodium fell to about 136. CT head when stable.
notes.body:
**Event**
At 1045 Maya told the RN her head "hurts a little" (2-3/10); neuro check unchanged. **At 1130** the RN found her harder to wake: **headache 7/10, vomited 100 mL, confused (thought she was at school), GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6)**, pupils 4 mm equal and reactive, moving all limbs. **HR 72 (110 at 1045), BP 134/92 (116/70 at 1045)**, RR 20, SpO2 97% RA. POC glucose 236 (on D7.5 since 1105). RN called me at 1131; at the bedside 1132.

**Assessment**
Meets bedside criteria for **DKA-related cerebral edema**: 2 major (altered mental status, heart rate drop of more than 20 not explained by sleep) and 3 minor (vomiting, headache, diastolic BP over 90). Timing (7.5 h after insulin started) and risk factors (new onset, pH 7.04, pCO2 16, BUN 28) fit.

**Treatment**
- **Mannitol 20% 24 g (0.5 g/kg = 120 mL) IV over 15 min, started 1140** through the right forearm IV with a filter.
- **Total IV fluid lowered by one-third to 100 mL/h at 1145** (same D7.5 ratio: Bag A 25, Bag B 75). Insulin continues at 4.9 units/h.
- HOB 30 degrees, head midline; ondansetron 4 mg IV 1140. Airway maintained; no intubation needed. 3% saline ready if no response.
- STAT labs 1140.

**Response**
1200: headache 4/10, GCS 14. **1215: GCS 15, oriented, headache 3/10, HR 96, BP 118/74.** Brisk urine after mannitol.

**STAT labs 1140**
pH 7.18, pCO2 21, HCO3 7.6; Na 134, **K 3.5**, Cl 106, CO2 9, BUN 20, creatinine 0.9, glucose 248, phosphorus 2.0, Mg 1.9. Anion gap 19. Measured osmolality 292. Beta-hydroxybutyrate 4.1. **Corrected sodium about 136 (was about 139 at 0220 and 138.5 at 0830): falling**, a risk sign for cerebral edema.

**Plan**
- **CT head without contrast once stable** (about 1255), PICU RN and I travel with her; insulin and fluids continue on transport pumps. A normal CT does not rule out early edema; treatment was not delayed for it.
- Neuro checks every 15 min x4, then hourly. Repeat mannitol (0.5-1 g/kg) or 3% saline for any return of signs.
- Keep total fluids 100 mL/h; no hypotonic fluids; sodium every 4 h (next 1630).
- K 3.5: continue 40 mEq/L for now; recheck 1630.
- Mother updated at the bedside; she called the father.

notes.title: CT Head Without Contrast
notes.author: Radiology Service (D. Park, MD)
notes.summary: No hemorrhage, mass effect or herniation. Ventricles and basal cisterns normal. No CT evidence of cerebral edema (early edema can be missed by CT).
notes.body:
**Exam**
CT head without contrast, 1255.

**Indication**
16-year-old in DKA with headache, vomiting, bradycardia and drowsiness at 1130, treated with mannitol.

**Comparison**
None.

**Findings**
- No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass, mass effect or midline shift.
- Ventricles normal in size. Basal cisterns and sulci open. Gray-white differentiation preserved.
- No herniation. Skull and sinuses normal.

**Impression**
No acute intracranial abnormality. No CT evidence of cerebral edema. Note: CT is not sensitive for early DKA-related cerebral edema; the diagnosis and treatment are clinical.

notes.title: Social Work Assessment - New Diagnosis
notes.author: D. Mensah, LCSW
notes.summary: Met mother (father driving home, arriving tonight). Strong family, insurance through the mother's employer, no transport or housing problems. High stress and guilt after the morning emergency. Supports, work leave, sibling care and school contact arranged.
notes.body:
**Met with** Danielle Thompson (mother) at the bedside and in the family room; Maya resting.

**Family**
Two-parent home with Maya and Eli (11). Father Kevin is a long-haul truck driver; he was in Ohio and is driving home, expected about 2200 tonight. Maternal grandmother lives 20 minutes away and is caring for Eli.

**Resources**
Commercial insurance through the mother's school district employer. Own car. No housing, food or utility concerns. Mother can take family medical leave (FMLA); papers given. Father's employer allows a week off.

**Coping**
Mother is tearful and exhausted (awake since Sunday). Strong guilt: "I bought her the sports drinks. I should have known." Very frightened by the 1130 event ("they said her brain could swell"). Reassured about the cause of type 1 diabetes. Maya is quiet and asked to sleep; will meet her separately tomorrow.

**Plan**
- Parking pass and meal vouchers given; family lounge and showers shown.
- With consent, will contact the high school nurse and counselor once Maya is out of the PICU (attendance, finals next week, 504 plan).
- Child life referral for needle coping (with diabetes education).
- Will follow daily.

notes.title: 12-Lead ECG
notes.author: E. Whitford, MD
notes.summary: Sinus rhythm 98, PR 140 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT/QTc 360/460 ms. Flattened T waves with prominent U waves V2-V3 (potassium 3.3 at 1630).
notes.body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 98 bpm. PR 140 ms. QRS 82 ms. QT/QTc 360/460 ms (measured to the end of the T wave; the U wave makes the end of repolarization hard to see).

**Interpretation**
Normal sinus rhythm. T waves now low and flat, with small rounded U waves after them, best in V2 and V3. No ectopy. Compared with 0300: heart rate slower (128 to 98), the peaked T waves are gone and a low-potassium pattern has appeared.

**Context**
Potassium 5.6 (0220), 4.7 (0430), 3.9 (0830), 3.5 (1140), 3.3 (1630) on the insulin infusion. Potassium in the fluids raised to 60 mEq/L at 1730. Recheck BMP 2030; keep on the cardiac monitor.
notes.impression: Normal sinus rhythm 98. Flattened T waves and U waves, consistent with potassium 3.3. No arrhythmia.

notes.title: PICU Attending Progress Note - Low Potassium and Phosphorus
notes.author: E. Whitford, MD
notes.summary: Neuro stable since 1215 (GCS 15, no headache). 1630: pH 7.23, bicarbonate 11, anion gap 17, BHB 2.6, K 3.3, phosphorus 1.8. Potassium raised to 60 mEq/L at 1730. ECG 1730: flat T waves with U waves. Glucose 186-198 on D10 since 1505.
notes.body:
**Subjective**
Headache gone since about 1400. Thirsty, bored, wants her phone. No vomiting since 1130.

**Objective**
Per RN: HR 95-100, BP 110-114/66-70, RR 22 (less deep), SpO2 99% RA, afebrile. Hourly neuro checks GCS 15, pupils normal. Voided 130 mL at 1600. POC glucose 198 (1500, **Bag B 100% = D10 from 1505**), 192 (1600), 194 (1700).

Labs 1630: pH 7.23, pCO2 24, HCO3 9.7; Na 137, **K 3.3**, Cl 109, CO2 11, BUN 17, creatinine 0.8, glucose 196, Ca 8.6, ionized Ca 1.16, Mg 1.8, **phosphorus 1.8**. Anion gap 17. Beta-hydroxybutyrate 2.6. Corrected sodium about 138.5 (rising again after 136 at 1140: good).

**ECG 1730**: sinus 98, PR 140, QRS 82, QT/QTc 360/460; **flattened T waves with U waves** V2-V3. No ectopy.

**Assessment and plan**
- **Hypokalemia 3.3** from insulin moving potassium into cells on top of total-body losses. **New Bag A and Bag B with potassium 60 mEq/L (40 KCl + 20 potassium phosphate) from 1730**: 6 mEq/h at 100 mL/h = 0.12 mEq/kg/h (maximum 0.5). Insulin unchanged (K is not under 3.0). BMP 2030. Monitor for ectopy.
- **Phosphorus 1.8**: common in DKA treatment; no weakness or breathing problems; phosphate continues in the bags. Ionized calcium normal.
- **DKA**: resolving steadily (gap 28 to 17, beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.8 to 2.6). Expect resolution overnight.
- **Cerebral edema**: resolved clinically after mannitol; CT normal. Keep 100 mL/h, hourly neuro checks through the night.
- Night team may allow sips of water if no headache or vomiting by 2000.

notes.title: PICU Night Progress Note
notes.author: J. Kowalski, MD
notes.summary: Stable night so far: GCS 15, no headache. 2030: pH 7.27, bicarbonate 13, anion gap 15, BHB 1.6, K 3.6 (up on 60 mEq/L), phosphorus 1.6. Sips of water since 2000 without vomiting. Glucose 170s on D10.
notes.body:
**Interval**
No headache since about 1400; hourly neuro checks GCS 15, pupils normal. HR 90s, BP 110s/60s, RR about 20 and less deep (per RN). **Sips of water allowed from 1945**: 120 mL since 2000, no nausea. Voided 120 mL at 2030.

POC glucose 176 (2000), 172 (2100) on D10 (Bag B 100 mL/h). Insulin 4.9 units/h.

**Labs 2030**
pH 7.27, pCO2 27, HCO3 12.0; Na 139, **K 3.6**, Cl 111, CO2 13, BUN 14, creatinine 0.7, glucose 174, Ca 8.6, Mg 1.8, **phosphorus 1.6**. **Anion gap 15.** Beta-hydroxybutyrate 1.6. Corrected sodium about 140.

**Assessment and plan**
- DKA resolving: gap 28 to 15, ketones 7.8 to 1.6. Continue insulin 4.9 units/h and D10. Next labs 0030.
- Potassium up to 3.6 on 60 mEq/L: continue.
- Phosphorus 1.6: no weakness, breathing normal; continue the potassium phosphate in the bags; recheck 0030. Treat separately only if under 1.0 or symptoms.
- Chloride rising (111) from the saline: expect the bicarbonate to lag behind the gap (non-gap acidosis). Not a reason to keep the insulin going once the ketones are cleared.
- Neuro checks hourly; total fluids 100 mL/h; sips of water up to 120 mL every 4 h.
- Father expected about 2200.

notes.title: PICU Night Event Note - Glucose Under 150 on D10
notes.author: J. Kowalski, MD
notes.summary: RN called 0305: glucose 147 on Bag B 100% (D10). Anion gap 13 and BHB 0.9 at 0030: acidosis nearly cleared. Insulin lowered to 0.075 unit/kg/h (3.6 units/h) at 0310. Neuro normal; father arrived 2200.
notes.body:
**Call**
RN called at 0305: POC glucose **147 at 0300** (154 at 0200, 158 at 0100), already on Bag B 100% (D10) at 100 mL/h; asleep, easy to wake, GCS 15, no headache. HR 80s, BP 108/64 (per RN).

**Labs 0030**
pH 7.29, pCO2 29, HCO3 13.5; Na 140, K 3.8, **Cl 112**, CO2 15, BUN 12, creatinine 0.7, glucose 160, Mg 1.8, phosphorus 1.9. **Anion gap 13.** **Beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.9.**

**Assessment**
The ketoacidosis is almost gone: ketones 0.9 and the gap nearly closed. The bicarbonate (15) is lower than the gap explains because the chloride is high from about 3.5 L of 0.9% saline (hyperchloremic, non-gap acidosis); this improves by itself. Glucose now drifts below 150 even on D10 because she needs less insulin as the acidosis clears.

**Plan**
- **Lower insulin to 0.075 unit/kg/h = 3.6 units/h (order 0310).** Keep D10 at 100 mL/h. (Protocol choices: raise dextrose or lower insulin, never below 0.05 unit/kg/h while ketones are present.)
- Call for glucose under 120 or a rise in ketones. Labs at 0430 as planned.
- Father (Kevin) arrived at 2200 and is at the bedside with the mother; both updated.

notes.title: PICU Night Progress Note - DKA Resolved
notes.author: J. Kowalski, MD
notes.summary: DKA resolved at 0430: pH 7.33, bicarbonate 18, anion gap 10, BHB 0.4. Glucose 152-161 on 3.6 units/h. Weight 49.1 kg. Neuro normal all night. Ready for the transition to subcutaneous insulin with breakfast (endocrinology).
notes.body:
**Overnight**
Slept between neuro checks; GCS 15 every hour; no headache, no vomiting. Insulin 3.6 units/h since 0310; POC glucose 152 (0400), 156 (0500), 161 (0600). Water sips 60 mL since 0300. Voided 120 mL at 0500. **Weight 0600: 49.1 kg** (48.6 on arrival).

**Labs 0430**
**pH 7.33**, pCO2 33, HCO3 16.8; Na 140, K 3.9, Cl 112, **CO2 18**, BUN 10, creatinine 0.6, glucose 148, Ca 8.8, ionized Ca 1.18, Mg 1.8, phosphorus 2.4. **Anion gap 10. Beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.4.** CBC: WBC 9.8, Hgb 12.6, Hct 37.4, platelets 248 (rehydrated; the high white count on arrival was stress).

**Assessment**
**DKA resolved** (pH 7.30 or higher, bicarbonate 18 or higher, beta-hydroxybutyrate under 0.6, gap closed). AKI resolved (creatinine 0.6). Potassium and phosphorus recovering.

**Plan**
- Keep the insulin infusion running until the subcutaneous basal insulin has been given (do not stop it now: ketones return within hours without insulin).
- Endocrinology to write the transition orders this morning; breakfast is the first meal.
- Hand off to Dr. Whitford at 0700.

notes.title: Pediatric Endocrinology Progress Note - Transition to Subcutaneous Insulin
notes.author: R. Banerjee, MD
notes.summary: DKA resolved. Transition with breakfast: glargine 20 units SC 0745, lispro 1 unit/12 g carbohydrate + correction 1 unit/40 over 150 at 0800, stop the insulin infusion and both bags at 0915. Carbohydrate-consistent diet. Teaching starts today.
notes.body:
**Data**
0430: pH 7.33, bicarbonate 18, anion gap 10, beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.4, K 3.9, phosphorus 2.4. Glucose 161 at 0600 on 3.6 units/h. Weight 49.1 kg. Hungry.

**Assessment**
New-onset type 1 diabetes; DKA resolved. Ready for basal-bolus insulin.

**Insulin plan** (doses on the admission weight 48.6 kg; estimated total daily dose about 0.9-1 unit/kg = 44-48 units)
- **Insulin glargine 20 units SC daily at 0800**; first dose **0745 today** (about 0.4 unit/kg; basal about 40-45%).
- **Insulin lispro with meals: 1 unit per 12 g carbohydrate** (500 rule: 500 / 44 = about 11; rounded to 12 for a first day) **plus correction 1 unit per 40 mg/dL above 150** (1800 rule) before meals and at bedtime. Half-unit pens; round to the nearest 0.5 unit.
- **Stop the insulin infusion and both two-bag fluids at 0915**: 1.5 hours of overlap with the glargine and about 1 hour after the breakfast lispro. Then D5 0.45% saline with KCl 20 mEq/L at 60 mL/h until she drinks well (lock at 1700).
- POC glucose before meals, bedtime and 0300; also 1000 today. BMP and beta-hydroxybutyrate at 1300 (rebound ketosis check).
- Carbohydrate-consistent diet: 60-75 g per meal, 15-30 g snacks.

**Education**
Diabetes educator today (survival skills), dietitian (carbohydrate counting), child life (needles). Goal: Maya and both parents each give an injection and treat a low (with teach-back) before discharge. CGM discussion tomorrow.

Discussed with Maya and both parents at the bedside: why both a long-acting and a mealtime insulin, and that the doses will change over the next weeks (often less insulin is needed for a while: the "honeymoon").

notes.title: PICU Attending Progress Note - Day 2 (Transition Done)
notes.author: E. Whitford, MD
notes.summary: Transition done: glargine 20 units 0745, breakfast lispro 0800, infusion stopped 0915. Glucose 154 (0745), 172 (0900), 196 (1000). Ate 90% of breakfast. Neuro normal; checks every 4 h from 1000. C-peptide 0.2 (low). Confidential HEADSS done. Transfer to 5 North this afternoon.
notes.body:
**Subjective**
"I feel like a person again." Hungry; ate about 90% of breakfast (60 g carbohydrate). No headache, belly ache gone. Asked to shower and to have her phone.

**Objective**
Per RN: HR 80s, BP 112-116/68-70, RR 16, SpO2 99% RA, afebrile. Neuro normal; **neuro checks every 4 h from 1000**.

POC glucose 154 (0745, before breakfast), 172 (0900), 196 (1000, 45 min after the infusion stopped). Per the MAR: glargine 20 units SC 0745, lispro 5 units 0800 (60 g / 12; no correction at 154). Insulin infusion and two-bag fluids stopped 0915; D5 0.45% saline + KCl 20 at 60 mL/h.

**C-peptide 0.2 ng/mL** (resulted 1000; drawn with glucose 612): very low insulin production, fits type 1 diabetes.

**Adolescent interview (HEADSS, alone, 1000)**
Home: close to parents; "Mom is freaking out." Education: honor roll; worried about finals next week. Activities: club volleyball, babysits. Drugs/alcohol: drank at a party once in October; no vaping or drugs. Sexuality: not sexually active. Suicide/mood: stressed, sleeping poorly; PHQ-A 6 (mild); no thoughts of self-harm. Safety: learner's permit. Counseled: alcohol can cause delayed lows hours later (overnight); check glucose before driving (must be over 90; carry fast sugar).

**Assessment and plan**
- New-onset type 1 diabetes, DKA resolved; on basal-bolus insulin. Expect some higher readings today after the infusion stops (insulin catching up); correct per scale. Watch for lows tonight.
- BMP and beta-hydroxybutyrate 1300.
- Neurologic: back to baseline after the possible cerebral edema yesterday; no deficits.
- Transfer to Pediatrics 5 North (adolescent unit) about 1500 if the 1300 labs are reassuring.
- Diabetes educator and child life this afternoon.

notes.title: Diabetes Education Session 1 - Survival Skills
notes.author: H. Lindgren, RN, CDCES
notes.summary: First session with Maya and both parents: what type 1 diabetes is, glucose meter, pen injection on a practice pad, symptoms and treatment of a low (rule of 15). Maya very anxious about needles. Plan: Maya gives her own dinner dose with child life; parents practice tonight.
notes.body:
**Present** Maya, mother Danielle, father Kevin. Learning style: Maya prefers short videos and hands-on; parents want written steps. Reading level fine; English.

**Taught**
1. Type 1 diabetes: the pancreas no longer makes insulin (autoimmune); insulin lets sugar into the cells; without it the body burns fat and makes ketones (DKA). Not caused by sugar or anything they did.
2. Two insulins: **glargine** (long-acting, once a day, like a "background") and **lispro** (rapid, with every meal by carbohydrate count, plus a correction for high numbers).
3. **Glucose meter**: wash hands, side of the fingertip, record. Maya did her own fingerstick at 1130 (268) with coaching.
4. **Pen injection** on a practice pad: attach a new 4 mm needle, prime 2 units, dial the dose, 90 degrees, count to 10, rotate sites. Maya cried before the first try, then did it well.
5. **Lows (under 70)**: shaky, sweaty, fast heartbeat, hungry, headache, grumpy, confused, nightmares or night sweats. **Rule of 15**: 15 g fast sugar (4 glucose tablets or 4 oz juice), recheck in 15 minutes, repeat if still under 70, then a snack if the next meal is more than 1 hour away.

**Teach-back**
Maya and her mother explained the rule of 15 correctly. Father explained why both insulins are needed.

**Plan**
- Maya gives her own dinner dose with child life support; mother gives the bedtime correction if needed; father gives tomorrow's glargine (with Maya).
- Session 2 tomorrow: glucagon, ketones and sick-day rules, CGM, school.
- Materials: new-diagnosis teaching binder, logbook, hospital video series.

notes.title: Child Life Note - Needle Coping
notes.author: K. Rios, CCLS
notes.summary: Maya fears needles (vasovagal at vaccines as a child). Coping plan: she controls the timing, counts down from 3, ice and pressure for fingersticks, music, slow breathing. Practice on a teaching doll; plan to support her first self-injection at dinner.
notes.body:
**Assessment**
Maya says she has always hated needles ("I passed out at my 12-year shots"). She is scared of "doing this four times a day forever" and embarrassed to inject at school. Her mother's anxiety rises when Maya cries.

**Interventions**
- Explained the 4 mm pen needle (shorter than a fingernail is wide) next to a vaccine needle.
- Medical play: Maya injected a teaching doll several times, then a practice pad.
- **Coping plan she chose**: she decides when (within 2 minutes), slow breathing (in 4, out 6), counts down from 3, earbuds with her playlist, ice on the fingertip before fingersticks, pressure after.
- Coached the mother to stay calm and quiet during injections ("one voice").
- Talked about telling friends and the volleyball coach (her choice); peer support: the hospital's teen diabetes group and diabetes camp in summer.

**Plan**
Will be present for Maya's first self-injection at dinner (about 1730). Comfort kit left at the bedside.

notes.title: PICU Transfer Summary to Pediatrics 5 North
notes.author: E. Whitford, MD
notes.summary: Transfer to 5N-12 at 1500. Summary of severe DKA, possible cerebral edema treated with mannitol, low potassium/phosphorus, and the transition. 1300: bicarbonate 21, anion gap 10, BHB 0.3, K 3.7. Lunch glucose 268 corrected.
notes.body:
**PICU course (Mon 0700 - Tue 1500)**
1. **Severe DKA at diagnosis of type 1 diabetes** (pH 7.04, bicarbonate 5, gap 28, beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.8, glucose 612). One 10 mL/kg bolus, then deficit + maintenance (150 mL/h, cut to 100 mL/h at 1145). Insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h from 0400 Mon, no bolus; two-bag dextrose; lowered to 0.075 unit/kg/h at 0310 Tue. **Resolved 0430 Tue** (pH 7.33, bicarbonate 18, beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.4).
2. **Possible cerebral edema 1130 Mon** (headache, vomiting, GCS 13, HR 110 to 72, BP 134/92): mannitol 24 g at 1140, fluids cut by one-third; normal within 45 min; CT head normal. No recurrence.
3. **Hypokalemia** (nadir 3.3 at 1630 Mon, flat T waves with U waves) and **hypophosphatemia** (nadir 1.6): potassium 60 mEq/L from 1730; recovered (K 3.7, phosphorus 2.6 today).
4. **AKI** (creatinine 1.3) resolved (0.6).
5. **Transition** Tue: glargine 20 units 0745, lispro with meals, infusion off 0915.

**Labs 1300**: Na 139, K 3.7, Cl 108, CO2 21, BUN 8, creatinine 0.6, glucose 212, Ca 9.0, Mg 1.8, phosphorus 2.6, anion gap 10, **beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.3** (no rebound ketosis).

**Glucose since the infusion stopped**: 196 (1000), 268 (1130, before lunch: lunch dose 70 g / 12 = 6 units + correction (268-150)/40 = 3 units).

**To do on 5 North**
- POC glucose before meals, bedtime and 0300; insulin per orders. Hypoglycemia protocol.
- Maintenance IV 60 mL/h until 1700, then saline lock if drinking well; remove the right forearm IV.
- Vital signs every 4 h; neuro checks every 4 h for 24 h more.
- Teaching (educator, dietitian, child life, social work). BMP Wednesday 0500.
- Weight 49.1 kg (dosing weight stays 48.6 kg).

notes.title: Pediatric Hospitalist Admission Note - 5 North
notes.author: B. Osterman, MD
notes.summary: Accepted on 5N-12 from the PICU: new-onset type 1 diabetes after severe DKA, now on glargine and lispro. Well, eating, neuro normal. Plan: insulin per endocrinology, teaching, discharge likely Thursday.
notes.body:
**Summary**
See PICU transfer summary. Arrived on 5 North at 1500 walking with her father.

**Exam 1545**
Alert, chatty, GCS 15, no headache. HR 80, BP 114/70, RR 16, SpO2 99% RA, T 98.6 F. Moist mouth. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Left AC IV with D5 0.45% saline + KCl 20 at 60 mL/h, site clean; right forearm saline lock.

**Data**
1300 labs normal except glucose 212; beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.3. Glucose 268 before lunch.

**Plan**
1. Type 1 diabetes: glargine 20 units at 0800; lispro 1 unit/12 g with meals + correction 1 unit/40 over 150 (meals and bedtime). POC before meals, bedtime and 0300. Hypoglycemia protocol (glucose tablets/juice; glucagon IM; D10 IV).
2. Lock the IV at 1700 if drinking well; remove the extra IV.
3. Teaching with teach-back for Maya and both parents; dinner injection by Maya with child life support.
4. BMP Wednesday 0500. Anticipated discharge Thursday if teaching is complete.

notes.title: Nutrition Initial Assessment
notes.author: A. Fairbanks, RD
notes.summary: Weight 48.6 kg (10% loss since August), BMI 18.3 (about 25th percentile). Needs about 2,200 kcal/day. Taught carbohydrate basics and reading the tray ticket. Stop sugary drinks. No restriction of food amounts: regain weight with insulin.
notes.body:
**Anthropometrics**
Height 163 cm. Weight 48.6 kg on admission (49.1 kg today after fluids); 54.2 kg in August: **10% loss in about 4 months** (insulin deficiency). BMI 18.3 (about the 25th percentile for age).

**Diet history**
Skipped breakfast often; school lunch; big dinner; 2-3 large regular sports drinks a day for the last month (about 150-200 g sugar a day from drinks alone). Likes pasta, chicken, fruit, yogurt. No allergies; not vegetarian.

**Needs**
About 2,200 kcal/day (active teen, catch-up), protein about 1 g/kg. Carbohydrate 60-75 g per meal and 15-30 g snacks (carbohydrate-consistent while learning).

**Teaching (Maya, mother)**
- What carbohydrate is (starches, fruit, milk, sweets) and that protein and fat have almost none.
- Reading the **tray ticket** grams and a food label (serving size, total carbohydrate).
- Meal dose = grams / 12, rounded to 0.5 unit. Practice: lunch 70 g = about 6 units.
- **Water or sugar-free drinks**; regular juice and sports drinks only to treat lows or for long practices.
- Food is not restricted: she needs to regain weight; insulin covers the carbohydrate.

**Plan**
Session 2 tomorrow (carbohydrate counting with real meals, eating out, sports snacks). Will screen for eating concerns (routine for teens with new type 1 diabetes).

notes.title: Pediatric Hospitalist Night Event Note - Low Glucose
notes.author: S. Iverson, MD
notes.summary: Woke at 0225 sweaty, shaky, with a nightmare; POC glucose 64 at 0230. Treated with 15 g juice: 92 at 0245, snack, 118 at 0315. Likely from the 2.5-unit bedtime correction (248) on top of glargine as insulin needs fall. No bedtime correction tonight; endocrinology to adjust in the morning.
notes.body:
**Event**
RN called at 0240. Maya woke at about 0225 from a nightmare, sweaty and shaky, heart "racing". **POC glucose 64 at 0230.** Alert and able to swallow: **4 oz apple juice (15 g) at 0232** per protocol. **0245: 92.** Snack (crackers and milk, about 15 g) at 0250. **0315: 118.** Now asleep; skin dry.

**Context**
- Glucose 214 before dinner (1730); dinner lispro by ratio + correction. Glucose **248 at bedtime (2100)**: **2.5 units of correction lispro** given per the scale, with a 15 g bedtime snack not covered by insulin.
- Glargine 20 units at 0745 yesterday.

**Assessment**
Symptomatic **hypoglycemia (64)**, treated correctly and recovered. Likely cause: a full correction dose at bedtime (rapid-acting insulin peaks 1-3 h later, overnight when she is not eating) on top of basal insulin, while her insulin needs are falling now that the acidosis and very high glucose have cleared.

**Plan**
- **No bedtime/overnight correction insulin until endocrinology reviews (order 0255).**
- Recheck with any symptoms; 0730 before breakfast.
- Parents (both present) were scared; reviewed what happened, that it was treated the right way, and that this is exactly the teaching they need for home. Father asked to learn glucagon.

notes.title: Pediatric Endocrinology Progress Note - Dose Adjustment
notes.author: R. Banerjee, MD
notes.summary: Night low 64 after a bedtime correction. Glargine lowered 20 to 18 units; bedtime correction only over 250 at half dose. Labs normal. Start Dexcom G7 today (teaching); glucagon, ketones and sick-day rules. Discharge Thursday if teaching is complete.
notes.body:
**Data**
POC glucose: 268 (1130), 214 (1730), 248 (2100, 2.5 units correction), **64 (0230)**, 92 (0245), 118 (0315). Weight 49.4 kg.

Labs 0500: Na 138, K 4.0, Cl 105, CO2 23, BUN 9, creatinine 0.6, glucose 118, Ca 9.2, Mg 1.9, phosphorus 3.2, albumin 3.9. **Anion gap 10.** All normal.

**Assessment**
New-onset type 1 diabetes on basal-bolus insulin. Insulin sensitivity improving fast (expected after DKA; a partial remission "honeymoon" often follows). Night low was caused by a full bedtime correction.

**Changes**
- **Glargine 18 units at 0800** (10% lower).
- **Correction: meals 1 unit per 40 mg/dL above 150; bedtime and overnight ONLY if over 250, and then half dose (1 unit per 80 above 150).**
- Meal ratio unchanged: 1 unit per 12 g.
- **CGM (Dexcom G7)** placed by the educator today, for teaching and home. Doses in the hospital still from fingersticks; confirm alarms with a fingerstick.

**Teaching today**
Glucagon (nasal 3 mg), blood ketone meter, sick-day rules, CGM alarms (low 70, urgent low 55, high 250), exercise and volleyball, driving. School Diabetes Medical Management Plan written today.

**Discharge**
Thursday late morning if Maya and both parents complete the teach-back checklist. Clinic follow-up Monday 12/14; educator phone calls daily for 1 week to adjust doses.

notes.title: Diabetes Education Session 2 - CGM, Glucagon, Ketones, Sick Days
notes.author: H. Lindgren, RN, CDCES
notes.summary: Dexcom G7 placed 1100 on the back of the left arm. Taught nasal glucagon (both parents demonstrated), blood ketone checks and sick-day rules, exercise and driving. Maya gave her own lunch dose. Ready for the school plan.
notes.body:
**Present** Maya and both parents.

**CGM** Dexcom G7 inserted 1100 on the back of the left upper arm by Maya (with help); 30-minute warm-up; app on Maya's and her mother's phones (follow). Alerts set: low 70, urgent low 55, high 250. Taught: CGM reads tissue fluid (about 5-10 minutes behind a fingerstick); **check a fingerstick when symptoms don't match the CGM, during the first day, or before treating in the hospital**; lying on the sensor can cause a false low ("compression low").

**Lunch** POC 176; Maya counted 70 g and calculated 6 + 0.5 = 6.5 units and gave it herself at 1200 (abdomen), checked by the RN.

**Glucagon** Nasal glucagon 3 mg (Baqsimi): for a low when she cannot swallow safely, is passing out or seizing. Put her on her side, one spray in one nostril (no need to inhale), call 911, give sugar when awake. **Both parents demonstrated with the trainer.** One device at home, one in her bag; the school nurse gets one.

**Ketones and sick-day rules**
- Check blood ketones when glucose is over 250 twice in a row (or over 300 once), or when sick or vomiting.
- Under 0.6: normal. **0.6-1.4**: extra rapid insulin (correction dose), 250-500 mL water every hour, recheck in 2 hours, call the diabetes team. **1.5 or more, or vomiting, belly pain, fast breathing, very sleepy: call now / go to the ED** (DKA starting).
- **Never skip glargine, even if not eating.** Sugary fluids if glucose is low and she cannot eat.

**Exercise and driving**
Check before volleyball; if under 120 eat 15-30 g first; carry fast sugar; lows can come hours after practice. Before driving glucose must be over 90 (check or CGM); never drive low.

**Teach-back**
Maya explained ketone levels and what to do; father demonstrated glucagon; mother explained the CGM fingerstick rule.

**Plan** Dinner: mother gives the meal dose. Tonight: Maya gives nothing at bedtime unless glucose is over 250 (new rule).

notes.title: Nutrition Follow-up - Carbohydrate Counting; Eating Concerns Screen
notes.author: A. Fairbanks, RD
notes.summary: Carbohydrate counting with real meals, labels and restaurant apps: Maya counted lunch within 5 g. Routine eating screen: DEPS-R 16 (cut-off 20) but she said she "liked losing the weight"; told endocrinology and social work; psychology referral recommended.
notes.body:
**Carbohydrate counting (Maya, mother)**
- Counted her lunch tray (pasta, milk, apple) as 68 g; ticket said 70 g: good.
- Labels and serving sizes; carbohydrate apps; restaurant nutrition guides; school lunch menu with carbohydrate counts (to send to the school nurse).
- Sports: 15-30 g snack per hour of volleyball; check before and after.
- Snacks under 15 g need no insulin; bigger snacks get a dose (1 unit per 12 g).

**Eating concerns screen (routine for teens with new type 1 diabetes; spoken with Maya alone)**
- Diabetes Eating Problem Survey-Revised (DEPS-R): **16** (screening cut-off 20: below, but not zero).
- Maya said: **"Honestly I liked losing the weight. Everyone said I looked good."** Asked if insulin will make her gain weight. Denies vomiting on purpose, skipping meals to lose weight, or plans to skip insulin.
- Explained that the weight she lost was mostly water and muscle from not having insulin, that regaining it is healthy, and that skipping insulin to lose weight is dangerous (DKA).

**Plan**
- **Told Dr. Banerjee, Dr. Osterman and the social worker** (with Maya's knowledge). Recommend outpatient diabetes psychology follow-up and a repeat screen at clinic visits.
- Dietitian visit with the clinic in 2 weeks.

notes.title: Pediatric Endocrinology Addendum - Antibody and Screening Results
notes.author: R. Banerjee, MD
notes.summary: GAD65 186, IA-2 42 and insulin autoantibody 0.9: positive, autoimmune type 1 diabetes confirmed. Celiac screen negative with normal IgA; thyroid normal. ZnT8 pending. Discharge prescriptions written.
notes.body:
**Results (drawn 0220 Monday, before insulin; resulted 1400 today)**
- **GAD65 antibody 186 IU/mL** (negative under 5): positive.
- **IA-2 antibody 42 U/mL** (under 7.5): positive.
- **Insulin autoantibody 0.9 U/mL** (under 0.4): positive (valid because it was drawn before any insulin).
- ZnT8: pending (send-out).
- **Tissue transglutaminase IgA 1.0 (negative), total IgA 168 (normal)**: no celiac disease now.
- TSH 2.1, free T4 1.0 (Monday): normal.
- C-peptide 0.2 ng/mL with glucose 612: low.

**Interpretation**
**Autoimmune (type 1A) diabetes confirmed.** Insulin is lifelong. Screen thyroid every 1-2 years and celiac disease at 2 and 5 years after diagnosis (or with symptoms). Siblings and parents can join research screening for type 1 diabetes antibodies (TrialNet); discussed with the parents for Eli.

**Discharge prescriptions written** (glargine and lispro pens, pen needles, meter, strips, ketone meter and strips, Dexcom G7 sensors, nasal glucagon 3 mg x2, glucose tablets). Explained to Maya and her parents.

notes.title: Social Work Follow-up - School Plan and Coping
notes.author: D. Mensah, LCSW
notes.summary: School nurse and counselor contacted (with consent): Diabetes Medical Management Plan and 504 plan meeting next week; finals can be rescheduled. Parents coping better; father returning to work in a week. Psychology referral placed for adjustment and eating concerns.
notes.body:
**School (Westbrook High School)**
Spoke with the school nurse (R. Delgado, RN) and counselor with written consent. The school will receive the Diabetes Medical Management Plan from endocrinology; **504 plan meeting** Wednesday 12/16 (testing and snacks in class, extra time for exams if glucose is out of range, access to water and the bathroom, nurse visits). Finals may be taken the week of 12/21 or in January. Glucagon and supplies to the nurse's office.

**Family**
Both parents at the bedside since Monday night. Mother slept last night for the first time. Father: "I'm on the road a lot; I need to know how to do all of this too." Brother Eli (11) worried; parents will bring him tomorrow to see Maya and learn what a low looks like.

**Maya**
Tearful about "being different"; does not want her volleyball team to know yet. Talked about choosing whom to tell; the teen diabetes group; summer diabetes camp.

**Psychosocial plan**
- **Outpatient pediatric diabetes psychology referral** (adjustment, needle fear, and the eating concern the dietitian raised); first visit within 2-3 weeks.
- Discharge supplies covered by insurance (case management confirmed).
- Will see the family once more before discharge.

notes.title: Case Management Discharge Planning Note
notes.author: P. Albright, RN CM
notes.summary: Discharge Thursday late morning home with parents. Insurance covers pens, CGM (prior authorization approved 1430), ketone meter and glucagon; copays reviewed. Meds-to-beds delivery; clinic Monday 12/14; educator calls daily.
notes.body:
**Plan** Home with both parents Thursday 12/10 after lunch teaching is complete.

**Coverage (commercial plan through the mother's employer)**
- Insulin glargine and lispro pens: covered (preferred brands), copay $35 per month each under the plan's insulin cap.
- Pen needles, meter, strips, lancets, blood ketone meter and strips: covered.
- **Dexcom G7: prior authorization approved 1430 today** (pharmacy benefit; 3 sensors per 30 days).

**Arrangements**
- Meds-to-beds from the hospital outpatient pharmacy: delivered to the room Thursday morning for the final check with the nurse.
- Pediatric endocrinology clinic **Monday 12/14 at 1000**; diabetes educator phone calls every day for the first week (glucose review and dose changes); dietitian at 2 weeks; psychology referral sent.
- Sharps container provided; disposal instructions.
- School paperwork via social work.

notes.title: Pediatric Hospitalist Progress Note - Day 3
notes.author: B. Osterman, MD
notes.summary: Doing well. Glucose 142-188 today on glargine 18. Felt shaky after a 30-minute hall walk (fingerstick 104, CGM 98 falling): snack, teaching about exercise. Teaching on track; discharge tomorrow.
notes.body:
**Subjective**
Mood better; joking with her father. Did her own fingersticks and her lunch dose. After a 30-minute hall walk with her father she felt "a little shaky" at about 1555.

**Objective**
Vitals stable (per RN): HR 70s-80s, BP 110s/60s-70s, afebrile. Exam normal. Weight 49.4 kg.
POC glucose 142 (0730), 176 (1130), **104 (1600, after the walk; CGM 98 with a down arrow)**: ate an apple (15 g); no treatment needed for a low.
Labs 0500 normal. Antibodies positive (see endocrinology addendum).

**Assessment and plan**
- Type 1 diabetes on glargine 18 units + lispro 1:12 + revised correction. The walk showed how activity lowers glucose; good teaching moment (Maya noticed it herself).
- Eating concern flagged by the dietitian: psychology referral placed.
- Discharge tomorrow after the teach-back checklist (fingersticks, CGM, pens, carbohydrate counting, lows, glucagon, ketones/sick days, when to call). Remove the IV before discharge.

notes.title: Pharmacy Discharge Medication Teaching
notes.author: V. Shah, PharmD
notes.summary: Reviewed every discharge medicine and supply with Maya and both parents: pen storage, priming, needle disposal, glucagon, ketone strips, sick-day plan. Teach-back complete. No drug interactions.
notes.body:
**Discharge medicines**
1. **Insulin glargine (Lantus SoloStar) 18 units SC every morning at 0800.** Never skip, even when sick.
2. **Insulin lispro (Humalog Junior KwikPen, half-unit)**: meals 1 unit per 12 g carbohydrate; correction 1 unit per 40 mg/dL above 150 before meals; at bedtime only if over 250, half dose (1 unit per 80 above 150). Give 0-15 minutes before eating.
3. **Nasal glucagon 3 mg** x2 (home and bag/school).
4. Glucose tablets (4 g each).

**Supplies** Pen needles 4 mm, meter, strips, lancets, blood ketone meter and strips, Dexcom G7 sensors, sharps container.

**Storage** Unopened pens in the refrigerator (do not freeze); the pen in use at room temperature up to 28 days; never leave in a hot car; never share pens.

**Safety** Look-alike pens: glargine is gray, lispro (Junior) is blue; check the label every time. Prime 2 units before every injection. A missed glargine dose: call the diabetes team.

**Teach-back** Maya and both parents described the pen colors, the priming step, how to store insulin and where the glucagon will be kept. Father asked about acetaminophen and ibuprofen: both fine; no medicine interactions with insulin found.

notes.title: Pediatric Hospitalist Night Note - Discharge Day
notes.author: S. Iverson, MD
notes.summary: Quiet night. CGM low alarm at 0210 (CGM 54) with fingerstick 132: a compression low from lying on the sensor arm; no treatment. Fingerstick 126 at 0300. BMP normal. Weight 49.6 kg. Ready for discharge today.
notes.body:
**Night events**
- **0210 CGM urgent-low alarm: CGM 54.** Maya was asleep on her left side (on the sensor arm), no symptoms. **Fingerstick 0215: 132.** No treatment. CGM rose to the 120s within 20 minutes after she rolled over. Taught again: confirm with a fingerstick when the reading and symptoms do not match; lying on the sensor causes false lows ("compression low").
- Fingerstick 126 at 0300. Bedtime glucose 206 at 2100: no correction (new rule: only over 250) and a 15 g snack.

**Labs 0500** Na 139, K 4.2, Cl 104, CO2 25, BUN 10, creatinine 0.6, glucose 126, Ca 9.4, Mg 2.0, phosphorus 3.8. Anion gap 10. All normal.

**Weight 0600** 49.6 kg.

**Plan** Discharge today after the 0800 glargine (Maya) and the lunch teach-back; IV out before discharge.

notes.title: Pediatric Endocrinology Note - Discharge Readiness
notes.author: R. Banerjee, MD
notes.summary: Ready for discharge: glucose 104-206 on the day ward, no lows since the bedtime correction change, false CGM low overnight handled correctly. Final regimen confirmed. Clinic Monday; daily educator calls.
notes.body:
**Data**
POC glucose Wednesday: 142, 176, 104 (after a walk), 188, 206; overnight 132 (0215, CGM compression alarm) and 126 (0300); **124 at 0645**. No lows since the change. Labs 0500 normal.

**Final regimen**
- Glargine **18 units at 0800** daily.
- Lispro **1 unit per 12 g** carbohydrate with meals; correction **1 unit per 40 mg/dL above 150** before meals; bedtime/overnight only over 250, half dose.
- Dexcom G7 with fingerstick confirmation; nasal glucagon 3 mg.

**Teach-back checklist** (Maya / mother / father): fingerstick and CGM, pen injection, carbohydrate counting, low glucose and the rule of 15, glucagon, ketones and sick-day rules, when to call: done by all three per the educator, dietitian and pharmacy notes; final review with the nurse this morning.

**Follow-up**
Endocrinology clinic Monday 12/14 at 1000 (HbA1c in 3 months; thyroid yearly; celiac screen at 2 years). Diabetes educator calls daily for 1 week. Psychology referral (adjustment, eating concerns). 504 plan meeting 12/16.

Discharge from the endocrine standpoint today.
